title: The Fiat Grande Panda is a cheerful city EV
text:
Story narration. That is what Fiat CEO, Olivier Francois, says that Fiat separates from the wave of new (mostly) affordable Chinese EVs. He is the same car, he has an instagram full of List contacts And happily admits that the new Grande Panda needs to be a box office success.
“Heritage is key,” he explains. “Our design is rooted in our inheritance, and that is not by chance. It is a good way to reassure our customers. There are new brands but, hey, come and go. We have been here for 125 years, and we are here to stay. “
As with Renault’s new 5, the Great Panda clicks with a palpable trust. With its pixels of video game references of the 80s, thick posture and a cheerful color scheme (without gray, by order of its manufacturer), the Panda manages to offer a Proustian race without seemingly retro. Credit to the exterior designer Francois Leboine and his team, looks especially fresh in simple steel wheels. (It is worth noting that Leboine did the R5 before leaving Renault).
“Panda” is registered in low -standing letters on the side, in case you forget the name of the car, and these can be completed with protective filling. The Fiat logo and the four -bar monogram, which arrived 40 years ago in the one, mix and combine in the seats, the ornaments of the doors and the wheel arc, and are sent with laser in the Pilar C. all Those involved, you feel that they have brought their game A. Including those unrecognized heroes in the product planning department.
In the United Kingdom, Panda prices begin at £ 20,975 for the red level of entry level, increasing to £ 24,000 for the high specification premium model. A cheaper 1.3 -liter hybrid will soon be carried out, but for now the approach is in the completely electric model, with its range of around 200 miles. This, then, is the car that promises to do for the EV what the time Nuova 500 He did it for Italian mass mobility as La Dolce Vita I was in sight in the late 50s.
Urban utility The masterful packaging is part of its DNA, but the original 1980 panda is the clearest inspiration for the new car. That was designed by the teacher Giorgetto Giugiaro, who is still alive and riding an 86 -year -old trail bicycle, and a man who rules out his contribution to automotive design as a mere “problem solving.”
